texts.preamble: Awaiz Asif Supariwala vs State Of Maharashtra on 29 September, 2025 Author: Amit Borkar Bench: Amit Borkar 2025:Bhc-As:41216 3-aba Shabnoor In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1008 Of 2022 Digitally signed by Shabnoor Shabnoor Ayub Ayub Pathan Pathan Date: 2025.09.29 15:28:47 Awaiz Asif Supariwala ... Applicant +0530 V/s. The State of Maharashtra ... Respondent Mr. Kuldeep S. Patil a/w Ms. Saili N. Dhuru, for the Applicant. Mrs. Rajashree V. Newton, App for the State- Respondent. Mr. Eknath Pandurang Sakpal, Psi, Dadar Coastal Police Station is present. Coram : Amit Borkar, J. Dated : September 29, 2025 P.C.: 1.
texts.facts: The applicant has filed this application seeking pre-arrest bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The applicant apprehends arrest in connection with Crime Register No. 54 of 2021 registered at Dadar Coastal Police Station, District Raigad. The offences alleged are under Sections 420, 328, 272 and 273 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and under Section 59 of the Food Awaiz Asif Supariwala vs State Of Maharashtra on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10765054/ 1 Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that on 6 December 2021, the police officials of Dadar Sagari Police Station received secret information that a tempo bearing registration No. MH/14/JL/5579 was carrying prohibited contraband while travelling from Mumbai 3-aba-1008-2022.doc highway towards Pen Taluka. Acting on this information, the police staff laid in wait on the highway. Around 4:15 p.m., the tempo was intercepted, and the driver was directed to halt. The tempo was brought to the police station, and two panch witnesses were called. On checking the boxes loaded in the tempo, packets of Vimal Pan Masala Gutka worth Rs. 25,27,323/- were found. The said gutka is a contraband item and prohibited. On this basis, an FIR came to be registered against the applicant. 3. The learned Advocate for the applicant submitted that this Court, by order dated 13 April 2022, had granted protection to the applicant. The applicant has not misused the [LEAKAGE_MASK] by that order and has extended full cooperation during the investigation. The investigation has now concluded, and the charge-sheet was filed on 22 June 2022. Hence, the interim protection deserves to be confirmed.
texts.arguments: 4. The learned APP opposed the application, submitting that the allegations are of a serious nature, and in view of the gravity of the offence, the relief of pre-arrest bail ought not to be granted. 5. The applicant was granted interim protection by order dated 13 April 2022. During this entire period, the applicant has abided by the conditions imposed and has not misused the liberty. This shows that the applicant has respected the process of law. 10. The object of Section 438 of Cr.P.C. is to protect a person against unnecessary arrest when investigation can proceed without custody. 11. Hence, following order: Awaiz Asif Supariwala vs State Of Maharashtra on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10765054/ 2 3-aba-1008-2022.doc c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any witness acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer.
